analysis: Examined the two supplied base_text units of ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler.swift (lines 1-1143). The changed head ranges fall mostly beyond these units (head ~1064-1068, 1167-1190, 1363). The patch excerpt shows a new `deliveredText` accumulator that tracks visible output only (content, reasoning, tool names and arguments). It serves as the cancelled-stream billing floor, so streamed tool-call hash markers no longer inflate it. Nothing else in the excerpt is a security control. The prior admission/drain/deadline/receipt-finalizer logic, decrypt, and fail-closed encryption in the visible base code are unchanged. Specifically: sender key length check; decrypt failure rejection; response-key setup failure and chunk encryption failure send an encryption_failure error with no plaintext fallback (T-008); privacy-safe logging of decode errors; cancellation registry cleanup. The new accumulator holds only text already in fullResponseText, so it adds no new disclosure surface beyond process memory (T-011/T-014, pre-existing). Billing impact is that a cancelled stream floor is computed from deliveredText. A lower floor could slightly under-bill tool-call-only cancelled streams, but that is not security-relevant and cannot be verified without the rest of the patch. Remaining uncertainty: the patch excerpt is truncated (the comment about the pre-content deadline for a streamed call's first fragment is cut off). I could not see how deliveredText is consumed or whether the deadline-handling change at ~1185-1190 and the change at ~1363 alter fail-closed behavior. A later pass should check that cancellation-floor usage and the deadline exemption for tool-call fragments cannot be abused to extend pre-content deadline holds (availability, T-010) or under-bill (ADV-001/ADV-002).
